subject: Service Assurance Anchor: uptime floor, tiered credits & maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Leslie Turner <leslie.turner@blueskyhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA: uptime/latency commitments for pilot & carveouts

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed with the procurement team, BlueSky is trying to lock down a standard SLA template we can use across our pilot and next-phase rollout. Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood commit to a baseline uptime percentage and a straightforward monthly credit calculation, and 2) we need explicit language around scheduled maintenance carveouts and whether those impact credits.

High level constraints: our security team prefers no more than a 0.5% monthly downtime allowance for pilot production traffic, but procurement expects a clear, capped credit to reconcile month-to-month. Also, we operate in three US regions and want maintenance windows to be regional where possible.

Can you share a draft SLA and an example calculation for monthly credits (including caps) so I can circulate? If there's a standard playbook for maintenance carveouts and latency SLOs that would be helpful too.

Best,
Leslie Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueSky Health

Attachment: MA_Window_Schedule.xlsx (stated schedule; stub)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Leslie Turner <leslie.turner@blueskyhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime/latency commitments for pilot & carveouts

Hi Leslie —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a clean first draft of a customer-facing SLA and a short worked example of how monthly credits would calculate under typical uptime bands. High-level summary below so you can share quickly with procurement/security:

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% per calendar month for hosted inference endpoints (equivalent to ~21.6 minutes allowed).
- Monthly service credits: tiered bands tied to % uptime (see attached PDF):
  * >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.9% - 99.95%: 5% credit of that month's hosting usage for affected service
  * 99.0% - 99.9%: 15% credit
  * < 99.0%: 30% credit, subject to monthly cap
- Monthly cap: credits capped at 50% of the monthly hosting charges (we can adjust for enterprise commitments).
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: planned maintenance windows communicated 14 days in advance do not trigger credits provided maintenance is limited to the announced window and follows a regional-scoped rollout (we recommend staggering by region).
- Emergency maintenance: emergency actions (security patches, critical mitigation) treated as carveouts if we can demonstrate necessity and communication within 24 hours of action; otherwise they are credit-eligible.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail 200ms for short-text generation (we call out latency credits separately in a latency SLA appendix).

I'll also include an appendix that shows a worked example for a month where Region A saw 0.12% downtime and Regions B/C were unaffected — pro-rata crediting by region and service slice is shown.

Would you like us to tighten the baseline to 99.97% for pilot if BlueSky is willing to accept a lower monthly usage cap on credits, or alternatively accept a higher cap in exchange for the tighter uptime commitment? Marissa and Karthik are looped to evaluate operational impact and cap math.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Draft_BlueSky_v1.pdf (SLA draft; stub)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BlueSky SLA options (ops impact & pricing)

Olga / Karthik —

Quick internal note before we reply:

- If we move baseline to 99.97% for the pilot, ops estimates ~12% uplift in reserved capacity to meet the more aggressive SLO across their expected peak patterns; that would affect price.
- Keeping baseline at 99.95% with a 50% monthly credit cap is lowest ops risk. We can do regional carveouts as proposed — ops recommends a max 2-hour single-region maintenance window (4 hours if rolling with 2-phase fallback).
- For emergency maintenance, we should limit carveouts to security-critical patches where a CVSS >= 8 is documented; otherwise emergency events remain credit-eligible. Adds discipline for later audits.

Suggested commercial levers to offer: a) pilot premium (one-time) to cover reserve uplift for 99.97% OR b) a smaller monthly fee uplift in exchange for 99.97% and a 30% credit cap.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success Ops

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: credit accounting and regional pro-rating mechanics

Folks —

A few accounting mechanics to lock down so procurement has a clean answer:

1) Regional pro-rata: credits should be applied to charges associated with the affected region's usage only. We'll need BlueSky to have per-region billing tags to isolate charges.
2) Calculation timing: credits processed in the subsequent invoice cycle; we can offer an interim statement if they want a quicker reconciliation for pilot months.
3) Crediting cap enforcement: the 50% cap is straightforward to compute (sum credits across bands then min(sum, 0.5 * hosting_charges)). If they want a split cap by region we can support that but it's extra complexity.

If we plan to offer the 99.97% option, ops + pricing need a short note on cost delta for the deal desk.

Karthik
Senior Product Ops

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Leslie Turner <leslie.turner@blueskyhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@blueskyhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime/latency commitments for pilot & carveouts (updated proposal)

Leslie / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we evaluated the options internally. Please find our updated position below (and attached redline PDF):

1) Baseline uptime: 99.95% per calendar month (default). We can offer 99.97% for the pilot period (3 months) if BlueSky accepts a deal structure of either: (a) a one-time pilot premium to cover reserved capacity, or (b) a recurring 8% monthly hosting uplift for the pilot period. Ops estimates the premium would be roughly equivalent to two weeks of hosting charges at expected peak.

2) Monthly credits (tiered):
   - >= 99.95%: 0% credit
   - 99.9% - 99.95%: 5% credit of that region's monthly hosting usage
   - 99.0% - 99.9%: 15% credit
   - < 99.0%: 30% credit
   - Cap: credits capped at 50% of the affected region's hosting charges per month

3) Maintenance carveouts:
   - Planned maintenance (14 days notice): carveout; no credits if maintenance stays within announced duration and scoped regionally. We recommend staggering across regions to preserve regional availability.
   - Emergency maintenance: carveout only for security-critical patches (CVSS >= 8) with follow-up post-mortem and evidence; otherwise credit-eligible.

4) Regional pro-rating: credits are applied only to charges for the affected region. BlueSky will need per-region billing tags to enable this (our billing team can help map tags during onboarding).

5) Latency SLOs: we propose a separate latency appendix; for short-text generation we propose a 95th percentile target of 200ms with remediation playbooks rather than immediate monetary credits unless there is sustained regression across multiple weeks.

Next steps: I attached a redline (SLA_Draft_BlueSky_v1.pdf) and a recommended maintenance cadence (MA_Window_Schedule.xlsx). If this looks reasonable we can prepare an enterprise amendment and route for signatures. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if procurement wants to walk through the credit math.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Draft_BlueSky_v1.pdf (redline); MA_Window_Schedule.xlsx (maintenance cadence stub)
